verdict_reason: The Marchenko-Pastur machinery is correct against analytic anchors I computed independently. _mp_cdf matches adaptive quadrature (scipy.integrate.quad) of the analytic MP density sqrt((t+ - t)(t - t-))/(2*pi*gamma*t) to max|diff| 5.6e-08 / 9.2e-08 / 4.4e-08 / 3.7e-08 / 2.2e-08 at gamma = 0.05 / 0.25 / 0.5 / 1.0 / 2.0 (worst 9.3e-06 at gamma = 0.999, right at the singular edge), with CDF(t+) = 1.000000000 in every case and the 1 - 1/gamma point mass correctly included for gamma > 1. The null behaves: iid Gaussian N=6000 D=300 gives outlier_frac 0.000000, spike_energy 0.000000, perm_outlier_frac 0.000000 and ks_distance 0.008658. Planted-spike recovery is EXACT: 3, 5 and 10 shared directions give outlier_frac 3.0/300, 5.0/300 and 10.0/300 and the permutation null recovers the same 3.0, 5.0, 10.0. The whole layer kernel is scale-invariant over 1e-160 to 1e150 (ks_distance 0.020426786 identical at every scale). replace_final_norm=True is correctly passed on both routes -- this IS a per-layer profile.
comparable_reason: mp_outlier_frac is a FRACTION OF DIMENSIONS, so with a fixed number of structured directions it is mechanically 1/D. Measured with 5 planted shared directions held fixed while D varies at N=20000: outlier_frac = 0.01953 / 0.00977 / 0.00651 / 0.00488 / 0.00244 / 0.00122 / 0.00098 at D = 256 / 512 / 768 / 1024 / 2048 / 4096 / 5120 -- exactly 5/D at every width. spike_energy is the width-invariant one over the same sweep (0.8624 / 0.8540 / 0.8573 / 0.8517 / 0.8537 / 0.8521 / 0.8545, a 1.3% spread), and the fixed-gamma ks_distance_g25 is nearly flat (0.8320 / 0.8265 / 0.8313 / 0.8282 / 0.8298 / 0.8285) where the gamma-matched ks_distance moves 0.9727 -> 0.8286. So the g25 family does its job -- where it exists.
normalized_ok_detail: It works but it is UNAVAILABLE on a quarter of the zoo. The g25 arm needs ceil(D/0.25) = 4D tokens and max_tokens is 20000, so it returns NaN for every model with d_model >= 5120. Counted against the 66 archived envelopes' hidden_dim: 16 of 66 models (yi1.5-34b 7168, gemma3-27b and gemma4-31b 5376, and thirteen 5120-wide models incl. qwen2.5-32b, olmo2-32b, phi-4, pythia-12b) would get NaN -- the large end the scaling claim rests on. I reproduced the NaN directly: at D = 5120, N = 20000 the g25 columns are nan while the gamma-matched ones are finite.
github_reason: Marchenko-Pastur and the BBP transition are classical results with no canonical released implementation for this use; the paper references (Marchenko & Pastur 1967, Baik-Ben Arous-Peche 2005) are theory papers. I verified the MP CDF against numerical quadrature of the closed-form density instead, and the bulk edges (1 +/- sqrt(gamma))^2 against their closed forms.
paper_reason: The MP law's own closed form is the published number and it reproduces: the CDF integrates to exactly 1.000000000 at the upper edge for gamma = 0.05, 0.25, 0.5, 0.999, 1.0 and 2.0, agrees with adaptive quadrature to <= 9.3e-06 (<= 9.2e-08 away from gamma = 1), and carries the correct 1 - 1/gamma atom at zero for gamma > 1. BBP: k supercritical planted spikes must produce exactly k outliers above the bulk edge, and 3/5/10 planted spikes give exactly 3/5/10.
confounds_reason: gamma = D/N and N is capped at max_tokens = 20000 for every model, so _meta_mp_gamma_* is literally d_model/20000 -- a pure width proxy (measured 0.0384 for the three 768-wide models and 0.0256 for pythia-70m at 512). It is correctly _meta_-prefixed. The emitted mp_outlier_frac family inherits a 1/D scaling by construction (exactly 5/D in the fixed-structure sweep above); mp_spike_energy does not. The task is absent from all 66 archived envelopes, so I could only measure this synthetically and on a 5-model panel where all mp_* columns did vary (sd 0.019 to 0.118).
defects: CONFIG: the fixed-gamma normalization is NaN for 16 of the 66 zoo models. fixed_gamma = 0.25 requires 4*d_model tokens and max_tokens = 20000 caps at d_model <= 5000, so every model at 5120 wide and above loses all eight *_g25 columns -- and those are precisely the columns that make widths comparable. Raising max_tokens to >= 4*max(d_model) (28672 for yi1.5-34b) or lowering fixed_gamma would fix it.

mp_outlier_frac (and its _cov, _g25 and lower_* twins) is a per-dimension FRACTION, so at a fixed number of structured directions it falls as 1/D: measured exactly 5/D across D = 256..5120 with the generating structure held constant. It should be accompanied by the raw outlier COUNT (or a count normalized by a null expectation), not only the fraction.

24 feature-eligible columns are emitted per run (three layer tags x eight statistics), several of which the source itself says are near-redundant ('the other two are also ~0.98 redundant with each other'). On my 5-model panel mp_ks_distance_mean, mp_outlier_frac_mean and mp_spike_energy_mean move together; no correlation-based demotion has been applied to this family the way it was to cka's debiased twins.

_meta_mp_perm_top_ratio_last is numerically wild -- 2.02 / 2.90 / 80.69 / 180.87 / 2.42 across the five models (sd 70.4) -- so any aggregate over it is dominated by one model. It is _meta_, but _meta_mp_perm_top_ratio_mean inherits the same behaviour (1.68 / 1.68 / 28.12 / 61.37 / 1.48).

The 'first/mid/last' tagging emits three tags even when they resolve to the same layer on a 1- or 2-layer model (the code notes this and keeps the tags for schema stability), so those runs contribute three identical columns.
fix: Raise max_tokens to at least 4*max(d_model) in defaults.yaml and the study config (or lower fixed_gamma) so the *_g25 family is finite for the 16 wide models it currently NaNs; emit the raw outlier COUNT alongside the fraction; run the duplicate-column sweep over this family the way it was run over geometry_cka's.
